Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
revision_notes: Cited source (Trading Economics, mirroring World Bank WDI SP.REG.BRTH.ZS) gives birth registration completeness of 25.7% for 2019, corroborated by the World Bank Gender Data Portal (25.5%, MICS6 2019) and the GFF/Chad CRVS knowledge platform (25.5%, MICS6 2019). This figure falls within the 20-49% band, not the <20% band used in the original scoring; the code is revised from 1 to 2 accordingly.
revised_comments: Birth registration completeness in Chad stood at 25.5-25.7% in 2019, according to MICS6 survey data reported by the World Bank and UNICEF, placing national coverage in the 20-49% band. Registration is markedly more complete in urban areas (around 50%) than in rural areas (around 21%).

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: National Biometric Population Register exists via SIGPTS system managed by ANATS, launched 2020 with biometric enrollment and ID issuance.
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and read. They confirm Chad's SIGPTS/ANATS National Biometric Population Register has been operating since 2020, deduplicating against a database of over 15 million people and covering identity issuance, voter rolls, refugee registration (since 2024) and school-based enrolment nationwide. A March 2026 article, however, describes the government as only now signing agreements to extend real-time interoperability from the register to other ministries, and notes Chad is ranked very low on the UN's e-government development index, which leaves some ambiguity about whether the register is best described as 'fully deployed nationwide' (5) versus 'partially deployed' (4). Because this is the maximum code on the scale, the score of 5 is confirmed but flagged for human review rather than asserted outright, per the top-of-scale escalation rule; no independent population-coverage percentage was found to corroborate full national deployment (that is tracked separately under reg-pop-uptake, not in this batch).
revised_comments: Chad maintains a National Biometric Population Register operated through the Integrated Population and Secure Documents Management System (SIGPTS), run by the National Agency for Secure Documents (ANATS). Launched in 2020 with Idemia-supplied biometric technology, the system deduplicates enrolments against a database of over 15 million people and is used for identity issuance, voter registration and, since 2024, refugee identification via National Refugee Identification Numbers. In March 2026 ANATS signed an interoperability agreement with the Ministry of Finance to extend real-time data sharing from the register across government, as part of Chad's Tchad Connexion 2030 digital transformation strategy.
